Shunt Location (?): ℹ️ Which battery cable the shunt is in. Negative lead: the Regulator Ground Wire lands on the shunt's load side, and the regulator corrects its voltage reading. Positive lead: the Regulator Power Wire lands on the shunt's load side.
How It Works

Rebulk: The system always begins in Bulk when charging is enabled. It returns to Bulk from Float or Idle if battery voltage drops below Rebulk Voltage or net discharge current exceeds Rebulk Current Threshold — continuously for Rebulk Debounce Time. The timer resets if the condition clears before the debounce expires. If SoC data is available, it suppresses rebulk when the battery is at or above the block threshold and permits it again when SoC drops to the allow threshold. SoC at or below the allow threshold also triggers a rebulk by itself, once each time SoC falls through it, without waiting for Minimum Float Time.

Bulk: The system pushes the maximum thermally- (and otherwise-) allowed current from the RPM Cap Table. Bulk ends once battery voltage has remained continuously at or above Bulk Voltage for Bulk Voltage Debounce Time.

Absorption: The voltage loop holds the battery at Absorption Voltage. Current is no longer commanded — the battery dictates how much it accepts and it tapers naturally as the battery fills. Absorption ends when current drops to or below Tail Current continuously for Absorption Completion Time. If the system is thermally constrained (the thermal penalty is meaningfully active and current is already near the tail threshold), tail detection is suspended until thermal headroom recovers — this prevents a false "battery full" exit triggered by the thermal loop pulling current down. If tail current is never reached, a safety exit to float or idle occurs after Absorption Timeout.

Float (if enabled): The system holds the battery gently at Float Voltage. After Minimum Float Time has elapsed, rebulk criteria are evaluated. Float also has a hard ceiling — if Float Duration elapses while in float, the system returns to Bulk regardless of voltage or current. (Idle has no equivalent timeout; only the rebulk conditions can leave it.) If Use Float is OFF, charging stops after Absorption and the system idles until rebulk criteria are met — better for lithium longevity in cycling applications.

Full Charge Detection

Full-charge detection watches battery current fall off, and no battery shunt is installed — so this card is greyed and full charge is never declared. Setup → Battery → Measurement Sources → Battery Shunt Present.

Battery Capacity (Amp hr) (?): ℹ️Total usable capacity of your battery bank in amp-hours. Set to your battery's rated AH at the 20-hour rate. This does not affect alternator output, it only affects the SoC display and rebulk logic.
Max Charge Detection Voltage (?): ℹ️Battery voltage must be at or above this level for full-charge detection to trigger. Set slightly below your Absorption voltage. If voltage never reaches this threshold during charging, SoC will never be reset to 100%.
Max Charge Detection Tail Current (%) (0): ℹ️ A percentage of battery capacity (A*hr), ex: 3% for 100A*hr bank = 3 amps
Max Charge Detection Time (s) (?): ℹ️Seconds the battery must simultaneously hold at or above Charged Voltage AND at or below the Tail Current before full charge is declared and SoC is reset to 100%. Longer values reduce false-positive full-charge detections.
Efficiency Parameters

These correct the coulomb count, which needs measured battery current. No battery shunt is installed, so the card is greyed. Setup → Battery → Measurement Sources → Battery Shunt Present.

Peukert Exponent (?): ℹ️Corrects for capacity reduction at high discharge rates. Lead acid: 1.15–1.35. AGM: 1.05–1.15. Lithium: 1.0–1.05. A value of 1.0 disables the correction. Higher values mean more capacity is lost at high current draws.
Charge Efficiency (%) (?): ℹ️Accounts for energy lost as heat during charging, not all current put in gets stored. Lead acid: 85–90%. AGM: 92–95%. Lithium: 97–99%. Setting too high overstates SoC; too low understates it.
Other Settings
Set SoC (%) Manually (?): ℹ️Force the State of Charge to a specific value. Use this to seed the SoC after a known full or partial charge, or to correct a badly drifted reading.
Battery Voltage Source (?): ℹ️The battery voltage that determines bulk, absorption, float, and rebulk. Control loops and protections always use the sensor on the regulator. Choose an external source if the Regulator Ground Wire is longer than 6 ft, smaller than 12 AWG, or if a shunt in the negative lead is not connected through Cable 2 pins 9 and 10.

Configuration
Nominal Solar Array Power (W): ? System-rated solar capacity, e.g. 600 for two 300W panels
Solar Performance Ratio: ? Share of rated output the array really delivers after tilt, shading, temperature, and charger losses. Learned automatically while Learn Performance Ratio is on.
High Solar Threshold (kWh): ? Forecast harvest a day must exceed to count as sunny. At least 2 of the next 3 days must clear it to pause the alternator.
Size Threshold from Consumption: ? On: a day counts as sunny enough when its forecast covers predicted consumption plus the margin below. Off: High Solar Threshold alone sets it.
Off On
Consumption Margin (%): ? Headroom added to the predicted consumption before a day counts as covered by solar. Larger values pause the alternator less readily.
Learn Performance Ratio: ? On: each day moves the performance ratio toward what the panels delivered. Needs a forecast and a VE.Direct link. Off: the ratio stays as entered.
Off On
Learning Rate (% per day): ? How far one day's result moves the performance ratio. Small values ignore a single cloudy day. Large values follow a real change, such as new shade, within a few days.
How It Works

Defer to Solar rests the alternator when the sun is forecasted to make up any charging shortfall in the next few days. The regulator downloads a solar irradiance forecast for your position, converts it to expected panel output using your array's nominal watts and performance ratio, and if the predicted output clears your High Solar Threshold on at least two of the next three days, it stops charging. The goal is to save fuel and alternator wear when it's energy the panels would deliver anyway.

Where your position comes from. Boat GPS (NMEA 2000) first. The location of a phone or tablet when the boat GPS goes quiet and the app has location permission. Or a position you type in, which is a sticky override that outranks both until you press "Use automatic GPS". Without a position there is no forecast, and the alert above the table says so.

Where the forecast comes from. The regulator fetches it straight from Open-Meteo, a public weather service. That request carries your latitude and longitude to their servers, and it repeats every few hours while Defer to Solar is on. This is a separate path from Cloud Features — the fetch continues whether Cloud Features is on or off. Turning Defer to Solar off is what stops it. If you would rather your position never leave the boat, leave Defer to Solar off.

When it refreshes. The download needs the field off for about 75 seconds, so the forecast updates while you are not charging — at anchor, or between engine runs. On a long motoring day the numbers above can be hours old; the line under the table tells you exactly how old. "Update Weather Now" forces a fetch on demand.

How it checks itself. Every day the regulator books what the forecast promised, what the panels delivered over VE.Direct, and what the boat consumed (from the battery shunt). With Learn Performance Ratio on, each day nudges the ratio toward the real array, so the forecast fits your boat rather than a typical one. With Size Threshold from Consumption on, the bar a day must clear becomes the consumption the last week predicts plus the margin, instead of a fixed number. The ledger and its chart are on Live Data, Integrations.

If the forecast goes stale. A forecast the regulator can no longer refresh — no internet, Access Point mode, a run of failed fetches — stops holding the alternator off once it ages past its refresh window. Charging resumes normally, the table is marked invalid, and the pause returns on the next successful fetch.

A device's name and software version appear once it announces them. Some devices announce only when they power up.

Nav, engine, and battery data in and out over the 250 kbps CAN backbone. That one port is shared: the Victron VE.Can and RV-C charge limits under Battery Charge Limits below arrive on the same wire, and they are decoded whenever the receive switch here is on or the follow switch there is. Receive NMEA2K Data and Transmit on NMEA2K are separate master switches, so either direction can run without the other.

InputReceive NMEA2K Data (?): ℹ️Input master switch. On: reads GPS position and time, heading, speed, wind, depth, and battery monitors from the NMEA2000 network, and decodes charge limits for display. Off: ignores all of that data, except that Follow External Charge Limits still reads charge limits while it is on. Transmit on NMEA2K is a separate switch.
Off On

Same setting as in the VE.Direct card, so only one can be on.

Displays list it under a separate instance, so you can put alternator amps on screen and set an MFD alarm on them.
Off On
Alternator Instance (?): ℹ️Must differ from the battery instance. Avoid 48 through 55 on a boat with a Wakespeed regulator, which uses those instances for its alternator.
OutputAlternator Temperature (130312) (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit on NMEA2K is on. On: sends the alternator temperature as a standard Temperature message (PGN 130312) that MFDs can display and alarm on. Off: does not send it. Sending stops if the sensor fails, so an MFD data-lost alarm also catches a failed sensor.
Off On
Network Label for Alternator Temp (?): ℹ️The value sent is always the alternator temperature. NMEA 2000 has no Alternator name, so this picks the name displays show it under, such as Engine Room. Point the MFD alarm at that name and the instance below.
Temperature Instance (?): ℹ️Instance number for the alternator temperature. Pick one no other temperature sensor on the network uses.
OutputExtra Temperature (130312) (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit on NMEA2K is on. On: sends the Extra probe's temperature as a standard Temperature message (PGN 130312) under the network label and instance below. Off: does not send it. Sending stops if the probe fails, so an MFD data-lost alarm also catches a failed probe.
Off On
Network Label for Extra Temp (?): ℹ️The location name displays show the Extra probe under. Pick the one that matches where the probe is mounted.
Extra Temperature Instance (?): ℹ️Instance number the Extra probe's temperature is sent under. Pick one no other temperature sensor on the network uses, including the alternator temperature instance above.
Send Charge Stage
OutputCharger Status (127507) (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit on NMEA2K is on. On: sends charge stage (bulk, absorption, float) and charger on/off as Charger Status (PGN 127507), so displays show what the regulator is doing. Off: does not send it.
Off On
OutputConverter Status (127750) (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit on NMEA2K is on. On: sends the charge stage (bulk, absorption, float) as Converter Status (PGN 127750). Off: does not send it. A Victron GX shows the alternator's charge state from this message, not from Charger Status.
Off On
OutputCharger Configuration (127510) (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit on NMEA2K is on. On: sends field drive percentage, charger mode, and enabled state as Charger Configuration (PGN 127510). Off: does not send them. This is the message a chartplotter or Victron system reads field drive from.
Off On
Charger Instance (?): ℹ️Charger instance number for this regulator. Avoid instances used by other chargers (shore charger, solar) on the network.
Charger Mode (?): ℹ️How this regulator describes itself when more than one charger shares a battery. A network label only. It does not change regulation or coordinate with another device.
Send Engine Data
OutputEngine RPM (127488) (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit on NMEA2K is on. On: sends engine speed as Engine Parameters Rapid Update (PGN 127488), useful on boats with no other tachometer source on the network. Off: does not send it. Leave off if an engine gateway or NMEA2000 engine already broadcasts RPM - two senders on one engine instance confuse displays.
Off On
Engine Instance (?): ℹ️Engine instance for the RPM and engine dynamic messages. 0 is a single engine (or the port engine on twins).
OutputEngine Dynamic (127489) (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit on NMEA2K is on. On: sends alternator voltage plus the warning flags below as Engine Parameters Dynamic (PGN 127489). Off: does not send it, so the flags below are not sent either. Same caveat as RPM: leave off if a real engine source already transmits on this engine instance.
Off On
OutputEngine Alarm Bits (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit on NMEA2K and Engine Dynamic are on. On: sets the standard engine warning flags inside PGN 127489, which most MFDs turn into pop-up alarms: over temperature, low system voltage, and charge indicator (a protection has cut the field while the engine is running). Off: Engine Dynamic is still sent, with every flag clear.
Off On
NMEA 0183Input ?

NMEA 0183 has its own protected serial input and its own wires, independent of VE.Direct, so both can be connected at once. Set the speed and signal type to match your talker, then watch the sentence count under Live Data → Integrations to confirm the link before trusting anything it carries.

InputNMEA 0183 Data (?): ℹ️Input master switch. On: reads heading sentences from the NMEA 0183 serial input. Off: does not read the port and clears any heading it supplied. This port has no output: the regulator never transmits on it.
Off On
Serial Speed, baud (?): ℹ️Must match the sending device, or every sentence fails its checksum. 4800 is standard for most instruments, 38400 for AIS receivers and multiplexers, and 19200 for a YachtDevices gateway. If the sentence count stays at zero, change this first.
Signal Type (?): ℹ️Normal suits a standard NMEA 0183 or RS-232 output. Inverted suits a bare 3.3 V or 5 V logic output. A wrong choice looks like a wrong speed: the sentence count stays at zero or checksum errors climb.
Victron VE.DirectInput ?

Reads a Victron battery monitor or MPPT solar charger over the VE.Direct serial port. Live values appear under Live Data → Integrations.

InputVE.Direct Data (?): ℹ️Input master switch. On: reads a Victron battery monitor or MPPT solar charger on the VE.Direct port. Off: does not read the port, so Use as Battery Monitor below has no data and the Victron readings stop updating.
Off On
InputUse as Battery Monitor (?): ℹ️Input switch, active while VE.Direct Data is on. On: uses the Victron battery monitor (BMV or SmartShunt) on this port as the regulator's battery monitor, for state of charge. With no shunt wired to the regulator, its current also ends absorption and triggers rebulk. Off: the values are still shown, but the regulator does not use them. Same setting as in the NMEA 2000 card, so only one can be on.
Off On
Battery Charge Limits

Obeying the charge limits a managed battery, BMS, or Victron GX publishes takes two parts. Pick the source in its own card, Victron GX or RV-C; a source card holds only what belongs to that source. Everything else is shared and is in the Charge-Limit Follow card at the bottom of this group. Only one source is followed at a time.

Victron GX (DVCC)?

Follows the charge voltage and current limits (CVL/CCL) a Victron GX sets with DVCC. Over VE.Can, the GX broadcasts the limits on the 250 kbps NMEA 2000/VE.Can backbone this regulator shares, and following them needs Transmit on NMEA2K turned on in the NMEA 2000 card above. Another alternator regulator on the backbone repeats the current share the GX sent it, in the same form as the GX's battery limit. With transmit on, this regulator sends a request when it joins that makes every device on the backbone announce its maker, and it ignores limits from any device that is not Victron. With transmit off it cannot send that request, so VE.Can limits are shown here but not followed. VE.Can has no bank filter, so the lowest limits any Victron device sends are followed, and the address of the device setting the voltage limit shows in the status row below.

Over WiFi, the XREG-010 app on the GX sends the voltage and current limits DVCC sets for this alternator, with no CAN connection needed.

InputUse as Limit Source (?): ℹ️Input selection. Makes the Victron GX the source this regulator follows, over VE.Can and WiFi. Follow External Charge Limits is the switch that starts or stops following. Same setting as Limit Source in the Charge-Limit Follow card.
Over VE.Can (?): ℹ️Whether the GX's limits are arriving on VE.Can, and their values. heard: within the last 20 seconds. silent: earlier but not recently. none heard: nothing yet, so check the GX is on this backbone with DVCC on. not followed, transmit off: shown but not used until Transmit on NMEA2K is turned on. Reads "idle" while RV-C is the chosen source.
—
Over WiFi (?): ℹ️Whether the XREG-010 app on the GX is sending limits over the network, and their values. heard: within the last 20 seconds. silent: earlier but not recently. none heard: nothing yet. Reads "idle" while RV-C is the chosen source.
—

VE.Can and WiFi carry limits from the same GX, and the regulator follows the lower of the two. The current limit arrives only over WiFi.

InputHold Stop-Charging Command (?): ℹ️What happens when a Victron battery sends stop charging, then stops repeating it. Off: the command expires after 60 seconds or the Silence Timeout, whichever is longer. On: charging stays stopped until the battery allows charging, sends nothing for the Silence Timeout, or the follow settings change.
Off On

Everything else this source uses is shared with RV-C and is in the Charge-Limit Follow card below: the follow switch, the CVL/CCL being followed and the follow state, settling and silence times, the plausibility window, trust reset, and raw frame capture.

RV-CInput ? · Output ?

Listens for the DC Source Status messages an RV-C battery management system broadcasts on the same CAN port, and that port has to be listening: turn on Receive NMEA2K Data in the NMEA 2000 card above, or the follow switch below. RV-C messages carry a bank number, so the instance filter here selects which battery bank is obeyed — the one setting that belongs to this dialect alone.

Transmit RV-C and the three message switches after it send this regulator's data onto the same port. They work whether or not RV-C is the limit source.

InputUse as Limit Source (?): ℹ️Input selection. Makes RV-C the source this regulator follows. Follow External Charge Limits is the switch that starts or stops following. Same setting as Limit Source in the Charge-Limit Follow card.
RV-C Battery Instance (?): ℹ️The RV-C battery bank number to obey. 1 is the main house bank. 0 obeys any bank heard. Ignored with the Victron source.
RV-C Messages (?): ℹ️Whether RV-C limit messages are arriving. heard: within the last 20 seconds. silent: earlier but not recently. none heard: nothing yet, so check the sender is on this backbone and the battery instance matches. Reads "idle" while Victron GX is the chosen source.
—
OutputTransmit RV-C (?): ℹ️Output master switch. On: publishes this regulator onto the CAN port as an RV-C charging source and sends every group whose Output switch below is on, so RV-C displays and battery systems can see the alternator. Off: sends none of them. Uses the same wire as NMEA 2000, so nothing extra is wired.
Off On
OutputCharger Messages (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit RV-C is on. On: sends Charger Status, Charger Status 2, Charger Status 3, and Charger Configuration Status. Off: does not send them. They carry the targets, the voltage, current, and temperature measured at the alternator, the charge stage, whether output is being held back, and the battery setup.
Off On
OutputDC Source Messages (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit RV-C is on. On: sends DC Source Status 1, 2, and 3 for the alternator: voltage, output current, and temperature. Off: does not send them.
Off On
OutputFault Messages (?): ℹ️Output switch, active while Transmit RV-C is on. On: sends the RV-C diagnostic message, a red or yellow fault flag plus a code, for protection cuts and sensor faults. It repeats every five seconds so a display can tell a healthy regulator from a missing one. Off: does not send it.
Off On
RV-C Charger Instance (?): ℹ️Which charger this regulator calls itself in RV-C messages. 49 marks it as an alternator. Change only if another alternator regulator on the bus already uses it.
RV-C DC Source Instance (?): ℹ️The DC source number the alternator is published under. 1 to 4 are reserved by RV-C for battery banks: house, chassis start, second house, and generator start. Use 5 or higher for the alternator.
RV-C Device Priority (?): ℹ️How much weight displays give this regulator when several devices describe the same DC source. 80 is correct here, below a BMS at 120.

Everything else this dialect uses is shared with the Victron GX source and is in the Charge-Limit Follow card below: the follow switch, decoded CVL/CCL and follow state, settling and silence times, the plausibility window, trust reset, and raw frame capture.

Charge-Limit Followsharedoff

Everything here applies to whichever source is selected above, Victron GX or RV-C, and the status row shows what that source has sent (for a Victron GX, the lower of its VE.Can and WiFi values). Received limits are requests: they can only lower this regulator's own targets, never raise them, and every local protection stays fully in charge.

InputFollow External Charge Limits (?): ℹ️Input master switch for charge limits. On: obeys the charge voltage and current limits (CVL/CCL) from a BMS or gateway on NMEA 2000, or a Victron GX over WiFi (DVCC). Limits can only lower this regulator's targets, and every local protection stays active. If the sender goes silent, the regulator returns to the targets set on it and shows a warning. A current limit of 0 A means stop charging. Off: received limits are shown but not obeyed, so leave this off to check them against the BMS or GX first.
Off On
Charge Limit Status (off): ℹ️Live limits and follow state. off: follow disabled (values still shown). waiting: nothing heard. settling: values arriving and being checked. following: limits in use. stale: sender stopped, own targets resumed. UNTRUSTED: a bad value arrived, and the sender is ignored until Reset Trust Latch. Confirm these match the BMS or GX before enabling follow.
CVL - · CCL - · from -

The trust latch is not set, so there is nothing to reset. This button becomes live if the charge authority sends implausible values and the regulator stops following it.

Reset Trust Latch: ℹ️Clears the untrusted state after you find out why the sender sent bad values. Turning follow off and on, or rebooting, also clears it.
Limit Source (?): ℹ️Which source this regulator follows. Victron GX follows limits a GX sets with DVCC. RV-C follows an RV-C battery management system. Only the selected source is followed. With several Victron devices, the lowest value of each limit is followed.
Silence Timeout (s) (?): ℹ️How long without a valid limit before this regulator stops following and returns to the targets set on it. With Stop Charging Without Limits on, it stops charging instead.
InputStop Charging Without Limits (?): ℹ️What happens while follow is on and no limits are being followed. Off: charges to this regulator's targets. On: charges nothing, though with a battery shunt it still supplies measured loads. Commissioning is not affected.
Off On
Settling Time (s) (?): ℹ️How long a new sender must send steady, in-range values before its limits are obeyed.
Voltage Limit Plausibility Min (V) (?): ℹ️Lowest believable charge voltage limit. A value below this marks the sender untrusted until the trust latch is reset.
Voltage Limit Plausibility Max (V) (?): ℹ️Highest believable charge voltage limit. A value above this marks the sender untrusted until the trust latch is reset.
Raw Frame Capture: ℹ️Shows raw network messages in the charge-limit ranges as text. Copy and send it to support when setting up a new battery system. Does not affect charging.
Open Capture
Minimal BMS On/Off Control

One wire from a battery management system (BMS) that says charge, or don't — any BMS with a spare relay or a charge-enable output can drive it. The BMS applies 5 to 62 V to the BMS on/off wire (Cable 2, pin 16) and the regulator takes that as permission to charge.

If your BMS or Victron GX also publishes charge limits, use Battery Charge Limits above as well: those limits taper the charge, and this wire stops it. Both can be connected at once, and the stop takes priority.

InputUse BMS On/Off Signal (?): ℹ️Input switch. On: the BMS on/off wire controls charging, as set in Charge When Signal Is below. Off: the wire has no effect on charging, and Signal at Input still shows its state.
Off On
Charge When Signal Is (?): ℹ️Present charges while your BMS applies 5 to 62 V and stops when the wire loses voltage, so a cut or unplugged wire reads as stop. Absent inverts it, for a BMS whose output energizes to signal a fault.
Signal at Input (?):
-
Data & Communication
Time Source (?): ℹ️ Where the clock comes from. Auto: NMEA 2000 time when present, then a phone or computer, then internet time. The others force one source. In access-point mode, a phone or computer is the only clock available. Position is set separately under Setup ▸ Boat.

Cloud Features needs an internet connection, and the regulator is running as its own access point. The switch below is greyed until it is joined to a WiFi network with internet.

Cloud Features (?):
Off On
Remote Diagnostics (?): ℹ️Lets support request this regulator's log files when you ask for help. Off stops the app checking for a request. Nothing is requested unless you asked for support.
Off On

WiFi Standby keeps the regulator reachable on your boat’s router between engine runs. In access-point mode there is no router to stay joined to, so it is greyed. Join a WiFi network above to use it.

WiFi Standby (Keep Reachable) (?): ℹ️Off: WiFi shuts off with the engine off, and you press the wake button or turn on the ignition to reach the regulator. On: WiFi stays connected to the boat's router in low power, using about a milliamp more, so the dashboard opens any time.
Off On
This Regulator
Name: ℹ️ The name saved under Setup ▸ Vessel Info. An unnamed regulator shows a name from its hardware ID.
—
Address: ℹ️ This regulator's network name. The name alternator.local reaches every regulator, so with two on a boat, it can reach either one.
—
Unit ID:
—
Connect To: ℹ️ Scans for regulators on this network and lets you choose one.
Regulators on This Boat
Add a Regulator: ℹ️ Lists other regulators on this network so you can mark one as part of this boat. Paired regulators appear together and first in the dashboard's list of regulators. Remove takes the pairing off both.
Settings Password
Password for Changes (?): ℹ️ Off: anyone on the same network can press Unlock Controls. On: Unlock Controls asks for this password. Live readings stay visible, and turning the alternator off never needs a password. If the password is lost, ground pin 11 at boot: that clears it and opens the WiFi setup page on the regulator's hotspot.
Victron GX
Live Link: ℹ️ A Victron GX reading live data now, its address, and how long it has been connected. Settings changes on the GX screen need neither Unlock Controls nor the settings password. The GX cannot run commissioning or update firmware.
—
Regulator Hotspot
Hotspot Name: ℹ️ The WiFi network name the regulator broadcasts in access-point mode, stored on this phone or tablet. Change only if you renamed the hotspot on the regulator's setup page.
Hotspot Password: ℹ️ The password for that hotspot. Stored on this phone or tablet.
Join This Network: ℹ️ Asks iOS to connect this phone or tablet to the regulator's hotspot. While on this network it has no internet, so cloud features are unavailable.
Display Preferences
Dark Mode:
Off On
Temperature Units: ℹ️ Choose Fahrenheit or Celsius for all temperature displays and form inputs. Setting is saved on the device.
Fuel Volume Units: ℹ️ Choose US gallons or liters for the fuel table, the live burn and economy readouts, and the fuel-used totals. Setting is saved on the device. Switching never changes a stored value.
Dashboard Update Rate (ms) (?): ℹ️ How often the dashboard receives fresh data, in milliseconds. Affects the display only, not alternator control. Changing it is not recommended, since several displays assume the standard rate.
Fast Channel Plot Sampling (?): ℹ️ Average shows the mean of each fast measurement. Max shows the largest sample, so brief spikes are visible. Applies to battery voltage, battery current, and alternator current. Use Average for normal operation and commissioning, because Max corrupts Voltage Control Autotuning.
Run Without Failed Sensors
A required sensor that stops reading stops charging. This screen is the only way to charge without it: each sensor can be ignored on its own, and the regulator says what protection that costs.
Sensors in use (?): ℹ️ Which sensors the regulator is currently running without, if any. Open the screen to change it, to see which sensor stopped charging, or to set a failed battery-temperature source to Not fitted.
Bench and Development
Hardware Present? (?): ℹ️ No starts demo mode and switches the field off. A simulated boat drives every reading, and once you switch the field on, its output follows those readings. Nothing is saved or uploaded, most settings are refused, and any setting you can change lasts only until you switch back to Yes, which brings back the real readings, records, and settings. The field then stays off until you switch it on.
No Yes
Protection Actuation Tests
⚠️ Fires a real field collapse
Deliberately trigger a field collapse to reproduce an electrical fault in a controlled way. The normal Live Data plots, CSV, and Console capture the transient. One test runs at a time.
1. Bench Testing (Manual mode)
For a manually-set field on the bench (Manual Field driving a power resistor). Hard-cuts the field you already set — no auto-energize. Set Field Control to Manual first; running without engine speed (Setup → System → Run Without Failed Sensors) is fine. In Manual mode the regulator's own lockout is bypassed, so the cut duration below is what sets the off-time. Set the values, then press Fire.
Cut duration (ms) (?): ℹ️ How long the field stays cut before your manual field is restored. On release the field ramps back at Duty Ramp Rate.
Repeats (?): ℹ️ How many cut / restore cycles to run (1-20). Applies to both the manual cut and the auto Ladder Walk below.
Gap between cuts (ms) (?): ℹ️ How long the field stays restored between repeated cuts. Set longer than the field takes to recover.
Manual field hard cut: ℹ️ Fires immediately. Cuts the field set in Manual mode, holds for the cut duration, then restores it at Duty Ramp Rate. Requires Manual Field on.
2. Engine Running (Auto mode)
For a running engine in Auto mode. Each Fire button first ramps the field up to the test current through the real current loop, holds until it settles, then triggers the protection. Refuses to start unless in Auto mode with charging enabled and RPM above Min RPM For Field, so it can never chop into a dead field.
Test current (A) (?): ℹ️ The field is driven up to this alternator current and held before the selected protection fires. "auto" picks a moderate level. Enter 0 to return to auto.
Instant field cut (hard over-voltage path): ℹ️ Fires immediately. Cuts the field instantly, then locks out briefly. The same instant cut is used for over-voltage, low RPM, over-current, critical temperature, and sensor-fault events.
Load-dump collapse: ℹ️ Fires immediately. Drops commanded current to zero with the field output left on, the fastest commanded field collapse.
Graceful ramp-to-zero: ℹ️ Fires immediately. Eases the field down at Duty Ramp Rate. If the instant cut or load dump test shows a fault but this does not, the problem is in the abrupt collapse.
Ladder walk (repeated cuts): ℹ️ Fires immediately. Repeats the instant cut using the Repeats value above, with the lockout growing from about 0.5 s to 10 s. Set Repeats to 16 to reach the 10 s lockout.
Abort running test:
Security & Maintenance
Physical Panel Override (?): ℹ️ Chooses who sets the charge rate and Force "Maintain Mode": this app, or the switch-panel wires on Cable 3 (Charge Rate on pin 5, Force Float on pin 7).

Off: this app sets both. On: the panel sets both and the matching controls here stop working. Charge Rate switch on is High, off is Low. Force Float switch on is Force "Maintain Mode".
Off On
Charge Rate Wire (?): ℹ️Live state of the Charge Rate wire (Cable 3 pin 5). Energized means 5 to 62 V is present: switch on, High charge rate.
-
Force Float Wire (?): ℹ️Live state of the Force Float wire (Cable 3 pin 7). Energized means 5 to 62 V is present: switch on, Force "Maintain Mode".
-
Lock Controls:
Erase All Memory: ℹ️ Erases all settings, WiFi credentials, calibration data, and buffered logs. Cloud registration is kept, so your account and history remain. To delete your account too, press Delete My Account first. The regulator restarts into WiFi setup, and you re-enter your WiFi name and password.
Recommend Initial Charging Settings
Works out starting values for the charge stages, the current limits and the over-voltage protection ladder from the battery type, capacity and system voltage on file under Vessel Info. Every row is listed with its current value beside the recommendation and you choose which ones to apply. Nothing changes until you press Apply Selected.
Configuration Backup & Sharing

Position, Speed & Course Sources ℹ️Where the regulator gets the boat's position, speed, and course. A phone or tablet running the XREG-010 app can stand in for a missing NMEA 2000 GPS. The clock has a separate setting under Setup → System.

Position Source (?) — live: ?: ℹ️ Where latitude and longitude come from. Backup: NMEA 2000 when present, otherwise a phone or tablet running the XREG-010 app. NMEA 2000 only: never uses a phone or tablet. Phone or tablet only: ignores NMEA 2000. A position typed in Setup ▸ Solar overrides all of these.
Speed / Course Source (?): ℹ️ Which source provides speed over ground and course. With Phone or Tablet GPS, the XREG-010 app sends GPS fixes about every 2 seconds, even in the background, which drains its battery. Speed records set on Phone or Tablet GPS are excluded from the speed leaderboard.

Performance Learning ℹ️Settings for the best-ever boat-speed learning system. The live polar / motoring display is under Live Data → Boat.

Speed source ℹ️Which boat speed to learn from. Water (STW, from a paddlewheel or log) removes current. GPS (SOG) is always available but reads fast or slow in a current. Switching erases all learned data.
Polar symmetry ℹ️Symmetric combines port and starboard, which fills the polar twice as fast. Both tacks keeps them separate, for a lopsided rig or instrument offset.
Reference ℹ️Learning keeps updating the best-ever reference as conditions are sailed. Frozen holds the current (or loaded) reference so it stops changing, useful to keep a known-good baseline while comparing.
Learned data ℹ️Clear All erases every learned point in both the sailing and motoring maps and zeroes the best surface points and hours counters. Use after a major rig, sail, or propeller change. Cannot be undone.
Tuning

A reading is only banked when conditions hold steady. Most inputs below come as a pair: a band (how much that value may drift) and a steady time (how long it must stay inside the band before the reading counts). Tighter bands and longer times give fewer but cleaner points.

Wind-speed band (kt) (?) ℹ️Max apparent-wind-speed spread allowed within a steady run. Wider accepts more data but blurs the map.
Wind-speed steady time (s) (?) ℹ️How long the apparent wind speed must stay within its band (above) before the run is recorded.
Wind-angle band (°) (?) ℹ️Max change in apparent wind angle allowed within a steady run. Wider accepts more data but blurs the polar.
Wind-angle steady time (s) (?) ℹ️How long the apparent wind angle must stay within its band before the run is recorded.
Sea-state band (° pitch std) (?) ℹ️Largest change in sea state (how much the boat pitches) allowed within a steady run.
Sea-state steady time (s) (?) ℹ️How long the sea state must stay within its band before the run is recorded.
Sea-state window (s) (?) ℹ️Time period used to measure sea state. Different from the steady time above.
Motoring RPM band (?) ℹ️Max change in engine RPM allowed within a steady motoring run. Wider accepts more data but blurs the speed-vs-RPM curve.
Motoring RPM steady time (s) (?) ℹ️How long the engine RPM must stay within its band before a motoring run is recorded.
Headwind band (kt) (?) ℹ️Motoring: largest change in headwind allowed within a steady run.
Headwind steady time (s) (?) ℹ️How long the headwind must stay within its band before a motoring run is recorded.
Min boat speed (kt) (?) ℹ️Below this speed the boat isn't really under way, so nothing is learned, which keeps drifting and maneuvering out of the maps.
Min wind speed (kt) (?) ℹ️Below this apparent wind speed, sailing data is ignored, too little wind to learn a meaningful polar.
Engine-off RPM threshold (?) ℹ️Below this alternator RPM the engine counts as off: on a sailboat the run feeds the sailing polar, on a motorboat nothing is learned. Above it, runs feed the motoring map.
Safety margin (kt) (?) ℹ️Higher keeps more points, including some that are not bests. The cloud later removes the extras.
Interpolation power (IDW) (?) ℹ️How the maps estimate speed between learned points. Higher follows the nearest points, lower blends more smoothly.
Prune neighbors (k, cloud) (?) ℹ️How many nearby points the cloud checks when removing a redundant one. Higher keeps the maps denser, lower trims more.
Reference validity radius (?) ℹ️How close the nearest recorded point must be for the % of best to be shown. Farther away shows "No reference here yet".
Local fit stiffness (?) ℹ️How much the local comparison resists following scattered data. Higher is steadier, lower follows the records more closely.
Learning-state risk threshold (?) ℹ️How much uncertainty is allowed before the panel says "Learning this operating region" in place of a %. Raise to show numbers in more conditions. Lower to be stricter.

How it works

What it measures. The fastest boat speed achieved for the conditions — apparent wind speed and angle when sailing, engine speed (RPM) when motoring — corrected for sea state (measured as how much the bow pitches) and wind. A sustained shortfall against best may point to a dirty bottom, poor sail trim, or adverse current (if not using STW).

Learned on the device. Steady-state capture runs about 10 times a second; the % of best comparison runs once per second. Instead of averaging nearby records (which reads falsely low at the edge of the conditions sailed so far), it fits the local slope of the best-ever surface through the nearby records and compares the present speed against that fit. The label under the % says what the comparison is based on — MEASURED (a recorded best exists for these conditions), ESTIMATED (interpolated between nearby records), or "learning" / "no reference" when there isn't enough recorded here to grade fairly (no number is shown). Two surfaces are learned independently: a sailing polar and a motoring speed-vs-RPM map.

Reading the plot. The blue curve is the learned best. The moving dot is your current speed for the conditions right now: it turns green once conditions have held steady long enough that the point is being recorded into the best (a steady run), and orange while conditions are still settling and nothing is being recorded yet. The status by the title mirrors this — Settling with a countdown of the seconds left before recording begins, then Settled once it does.

Pruned in the cloud (optional). About every 15 minutes, engine off and system online, new points upload and the cloud prunes redundant interior points back to the envelope, then returns the cleaned set.

Learning — ℹ️Turn off under tow, or in strong current with no water-speed log, to keep bad data out of the map. Stays off across reboots.

Counts of protection events since boot or last reset. All counters are rising-edge — each number represents how many times that protection mechanism activated, not how long it was active. Use the per-category reset buttons to establish a clean baseline after tuning changes or suspected transient conditions. FastOV events are normal during load transients; sustained accumulation at idle is not.

Voltage & Current Protection

FastOV Cap (live) ℹ️ Live limit on commanded current from the over-voltage protection (A). Equals the current limit when inactive. ? A
Protection Events (total) ℹ️ Times any protection has activated: Group 1, 2, 3, or 5. Slow growth during changes is normal. Fast growth at steady state means thresholds need tuning. ?
FastOV Hard Events ℹ️ Times Group 1 or Group 2 over-voltage activated. Should be rare. Growth at steady state means real overshoot. ?
iExcess Events ℹ️ Times the Group 3 over-current detectors tripped. ?
Voltage D-Term Engagements ℹ️ Times the voltage damper trimmed current during a fast voltage rise, which is not a trip. ?
INA228 OV Events ℹ️ Times the hardware over-voltage shutdown fired. Should be zero. A nonzero count means software failed to protect. ?
Hard OC Events ℹ️ Times the hard over-current trip fired. Field cut immediately. Should be zero. ?
Voltage Spike Events ℹ️ Times battery voltage exceeded Alternator Hard Shutdown Voltage. Field cut immediately. Should be zero. ?
Timed OV Cuts (Low Tier) ℹ️ Times battery voltage stayed above the low-tier line for its time to act, and the field was cut. ?
Timed OV Cuts (Mid Tier) ℹ️ Times battery voltage stayed above the mid-tier line for its time to act, and the field was cut. Should be rare. ?
Volt Disagree Critical Events ℹ️ Times the two battery voltage readings disagreed past the critical limit, cutting the field. Points to a sensor or wiring fault. ?
Volt Disagree Warning Events ℹ️ Times the two battery voltage readings disagreed past the warning limit. Field ramps down and can recover. ?
Volt Implausible Events ℹ️ Times a voltage reading fell outside the expected range. Points to a hardware or calibration fault. ?
Current Sensor Stale Events ℹ️ Times the alternator current sensor stopped updating, cutting the field after 10 s. Check the clamp sensor wiring. ?
Battery Voltage Stale Events ℹ️ Times the main battery voltage reading stopped and the field was cut. Check the battery voltage sense wiring. ?
Second Voltage Stale Events ℹ️ Times the second battery voltage reading stopped and the field ramped off. Check the second voltage sense wiring. ?
Battery Temperature Lost Events ℹ️ Times charging stopped because the battery temperature source stopped reporting. Check the probe or network source, or set the source to Not fitted. ?
Drive Temperature Lost Events ℹ️ Times charging stopped because the regulator's drive temperature reading was lost for 10 s. The field stays off until it reads again. ?

Thermal Protection Events

Temp Critical Events ℹ️ Times alternator temperature passed the critical limit, cutting the field immediately. Should be rare. ?
Temp Sustained Events ℹ️ Times alternator temperature stayed in the warning zone long enough for a shutdown. ?
Temp Stale Events ℹ️ Times the temperature sensor stopped updating, cutting the field. Check the sensor wiring if nonzero. ?

Oscillation Damper
How It Works

Some engine, alternator and belt combinations develop a slow wobble, somewhere between about 0.3 and 2.5 Hz, in field drive, engine speed and voltage together. This damper watches field drive for it while speed is steady, makes a single test cut in the current loop's integral gain, and retains the cut (at that speed) only if the wobble significantly shrinks.

The damper also has a second lever, for a wobble that keeps the voltage damper (the D-term) rhythmically switching direction. This is tested by pausing the D-term instead — if the wobble significantly reduces, the change is kept.

Status —
Oscillation Damper ℹ️Same switch as Setup ▸ Alternator ▸ Tuning ▸ Current ▸ Controller Parameters, where its settings are. On: the damper tests a detected wobble, maps confirmed trouble spots by engine speed, and applies the fix there. Off: full strength always, and the learned map is kept but not applied.
Off On

Wobble frequency ℹ️ Frequency of the most recent confirmed wobble, in cycles per second. It stays on screen after the episode ends, so it is live only while Status says a wobble is being damped. —
Voltage damper (D-term) ℹ️ The regulator's fast voltage damper. Normally Running. It can be paused during a test, and stays off across a confirmed trouble spot, shown purple on the plot. —
Episodes on record ℹ️ Each entry shows the wobble when the episode opened and closed: field swing is how far field drive was swinging, and gain left at is where the current loop's gain stood at the end. Survives restarts, holding about the last hundred episodes. Raw file: open —

Dots are the evidence: filled blue at the speed of each verified episode, hollow amber where a wobble did not respond, hollow grey where the test was interrupted and settled nothing either way. Control Accuracy

Each loop reports how it performs during normal running — no test needed. Tracking is the share of challenged time (target moving, or just after a disturbance) spent inside the accuracy band — quiet steady running earns nothing here. Excursions counts how often the loop left its band, with the average time it took to get back. Time when the output was pinned at a limit or a protection held it is set aside as "constrained" (shown in the small line) rather than blamed on the loop. A dash means not observed yet — never perfection. Accumulates since the last reset; auto-resets after each daily cloud snapshot, or press Reset below.

About this Alternator Diag Page

This subtab is the health station for the charging system — the alternator, its rectifier and belt drive, and the control loops driving them. Everything here is results; the detection gates and tuning knobs live in Setup → Alternator → Diag.

Shortcut to the Diag gates & tuning knobs →

Charging System Health grades today's alternator output against the best it's ever done under the same conditions. The engine-hours trend is the plot to watch: a healthy system holds roughly flat in the mid-90s+, and a steady downward slope is an early warning. The "This Session" plot below it shows the same grading data "live" since the page was opened.

Live Oscilloscope & Historical Snapshots shows the alternator's output current sampled at 20khz — fast enough to see individual rectifier pulses. Reference pages are known-good waveforms frozen once per RPM band; anomaly captures are saved automatically when the fault monitor trips. When something looks off, flip between the capture and a close reference for that speed and compare.

Resonance & Ripple Map is a learned table of the strongest ripple tone at every speed and load — used by the commissioning wizard to help optimize signal filters and control response.

Wear Rate & Component Life estimates how fast the alternator is aging at the present speed and temperature, and roughly how much component life remains (based on physics, but not yet calibrated…)

Control Accuracy reports how each loop — current, voltage, thermal — performs during normal running: time-in-band while challenged, and how often it leaves its band and how fast it recovers. Quiet steady running earns nothing, and time spent pinned at a limit is reported separately instead of blamed on the loop.

Is an anomaly alert a confirmed failure? No. The fault class is the monitor's best guess from the ripple pattern. Treat it as a prompt to compare the anomaly capture against the reference page for that RPM band before touching hardware.

Does it need anything from me? No — everything on this page learns on its own during ordinary steady running. A new install shows gaps and "learning" labels until the engine has spent time at more speeds and loads.

Replaced the alternator, regulator, or belt? Reset the learned baselines so old data doesn't grade the new hardware: Start Over (health matrix, in Setup → Alternator → Diag), Re-baseline (reference pages), and Clear Map (ripple map).

Battery Wear Record

How long the battery has spent at each voltage, temperature, and state of charge, how much charge went in and out at each rate and temperature, and how deep its cycles were, whatever the charge source. High voltage, heat, sitting full or nearly empty, and charging in the cold are what wear a battery out. The record survives restarts, firmware updates, and power cuts. Clear it with Clear Wear Record below when the battery is replaced.

—
Time at voltage and battery temperature ℹ️ How long the battery has spent at each voltage (measured at the battery), split by battery temperature. High voltage and heat together age a battery fastest, so time near the top of the table and in the hot columns matters most. Avg A is the average battery current at that voltage (+ charging). Alt is the share of that time the alternator was producing current; high voltage with a low Alt share came from another charge source, such as solar or shore power.
Time at state of charge and battery temperature ℹ️ How long the battery has spent at each state of charge, split by battery temperature. Lithium batteries age fastest when held full and warm, and lead-acid batteries lose capacity when left partly charged. Off is time the regulator was not running, listed against the state of charge it last saw.
Charge in by rate and battery temperature (Ah) ℹ️ Amp-hours put into the battery, by charge rate and battery temperature. Rate is in C, the current as a fraction of battery capacity: 0.5 C on a 400 Ah battery is 200 A. The Amps column uses the battery capacity in your settings. Fast charging in the cold wears lithium batteries fastest, and most must not be charged below freezing at all. Each rate is split by the state of charge the battery was at, because fast charging near full is harder on a battery than fast charging when it is low. The Alt column is the share the alternator may have supplied. The regulator measures the alternator but not solar or shore power, so when both charge at once the alternator is counted first, up to its whole output. Pick Alternator or Other sources to see either one alone.
Charge out by rate and battery temperature (Ah) ℹ️ Amp-hours drawn from the battery, by discharge rate and battery temperature. Heavy loads, such as an inverter, show in the higher rates.
Cycle depth ℹ️ Each discharge and recharge swing, counted by how far the state of charge moved. Deep cycles wear a battery much faster than shallow ones, so two batteries with the same charge throughput can age very differently. A cycle is a discharge and its recharge; a swing with no matching return counts as half. Avg middle is the state of charge halfway through the swing. Swings under 2% are not counted.
Time between full charges ℹ️ How long the battery went between full charges (99% state of charge or more), including time the regulator was off. Lead-acid batteries lose capacity the longer they go without a full charge, and lithium batteries need one now and then to balance their cells and keep the state of charge reading accurate.

Capacity tracker settings

Measured capacity needs an independent low state-of-charge anchor from a rested voltage. Edit the rested open-circuit-voltage curve for your bank (a chemistry preset is filled in when you save Vessel Info; the buttons below reload one), scaled to your nominal voltage. On lithium (LiFePO4) only the flat curve's bottom-knee rows map reliably to charge, so the anchor is taken there (≤20%); lead-acid and AGM slope across the whole range, so the anchor can sit at a shallower, non-damaging rest — the anchor window is set per chemistry.

About this Battery Diag Page

This page tracks how the battery bank is aging, from two independent signals: an internal-resistance test you run on demand, and a capacity estimate captured automatically each time the bank reaches full charge. The bank is assumed brand-new when first installed — the first capacity reading becomes the 100% baseline.

Resistance Test (DCIR) steps the charge current up and down with the engine running and measures how far the battery voltage moves for a known change in current. Rising resistance over months is an early aging signal. The absolute number depends on temperature and state of charge, so compare runs taken under similar conditions; the trend matters more than any single value.

Capacity Trend: each time the bank charges from a low point all the way to full, the amp-hours returned are extrapolated to a full 0–100% span and plotted. A falling line is real capacity fade. Only deep charges qualify, so the plot fills in slowly.

Battery Wear Record adds up, from the first day, the time the battery spends at each voltage, temperature and state of charge, and the charge that goes in and out at each rate and temperature. The voltage and temperature tables need no battery current sensor. The state-of-charge and charge tables fill from a battery shunt or a battery monitor on NMEA 2000 or VE.Direct, and stay empty with neither.

Replaced the bank? Press Start Over in the Resistance Test section — the next capacity reading becomes the new 100% baseline, and the wear record starts over.

Note: lots of better functionality is planned for future versions of this page.

Timestamps show when messages were received by the app, not when sent by the regulator. Messages are throttled: max 5 every 700ms (adjustable in firmware).
ℹ️ Downloads diagnostic logs as CSV files: temperature (up to about 2 hours), control loop (about 30 seconds, or about 8 seconds in Manual mode), voltage tuning (about 80 seconds), and with NMEA 2000, a bus-health log (24 hours). Logs clear after download. Pause Logs freezes them, and the dot is green while recording and amber when paused. Start Fresh Log clears them and starts over.
Filename Tag (optional) ℹ️Optional text added to the end of downloaded log filenames. Spaces and unusual characters become dashes. Leave blank for none.
Time Window: ℹ️Sets how many seconds of live data all four short-term plots show on the X axis. The highlighted button is the current setting. To set the Y axis range, click the top or bottom number on that axis.
Time Axis Labels (?): ℹ️ UNIX: Proper time labels, but slower
Relative: "Seconds ago" labels, but smoother plotting

Plant Delay Test

Plant Delay Measurement

This test measures how quickly the alternator's output responds to a change. It first ramps the field to your Wave Floor and holds there for 5 seconds to establish a stable baseline. It then steps the field up by your Wave Amplitude (in % duty) and back down, repeating that up-and-down step several times, timing how fast the output settles after each move.

This test measures the alternator's frequency response — an open-loop frequency-by-frequency map of the plant (a Bode plot). It first ramps the field to your Wave Floor and holds there for 5 seconds to establish a stable baseline. It then drives a swept sine on the field — from Sweep Start up to Sweep End, with the PID off — and measures the output's gain and phase lag at each frequency. The result shows how fast the field can move the output and where the plant rolls off.

⚠️ Bring the engine to your typical operating RPM before clicking Start. The test is most accurate at normal cruising speed.

⚠️ Keep Wave Amplitude small. Each upward step pushes output above the wave floor, which briefly raises battery voltage. Choose a value small enough that the test won't over-volt your battery — start low (a few % duty) and only increase it if the measured response is too noisy.

⚠️ Keep Wave Amplitude small. The sine swings upward from the wave floor by up to twice this amplitude, briefly raising battery voltage at each peak. Choose a value small enough that the test won't over-volt your battery — start low (a few % duty) and only increase it if the response is too noisy.

Results

Check the output current plot (behind this panel) for a clean square-wave shape. Ideal signals have sharp step edges with no more than ±1–2 A of ripple. Engines can resonate at certain RPMs — if noise is high, re-run at a slightly different speed.

Signal Quality ℹ️ Measured from the quiet period before each step. Green is good, yellow marginal, red poor. High noise makes results unreliable.
Step size ℹ️ How many amps the step command added. Larger steps produce a cleaner signal. Should be >10 A for reliable results. Noise (p-p) ℹ️ Current swing in the quiet period before the step, often from belt or alternator resonance. Under 1 A is ideal. Under 2 A is acceptable.
Timing Results ℹ️ Time from the duty step until output current crossed the detection threshold. Rise is the step-up response, fall is the step-down response.
Rise (ms) Fall (ms)
Frequency Response (open-loop plant Bode) ℹ️ Measured alternator response at each frequency, with the control loop off. The −3 dB point (gain about 0.71×) is its bandwidth.
Freq (Hz) Gain (rel) Phase lag (°)

FYI Note:
Automatic Maintenance Restarts

The regulator periodically reboots itself. There is no fixed schedule: it generally takes advantage of non-interrupting moments and forces an immediate reboot only if one wasn't found.

1
Starting after day 1 — only when nothing at all is happening
All must be true at once for a full 5 minutes: engine off, not charging, nobody connected to the app or dashboard, cloud uploads finished, SOC above 30% if it is known, and battery voltage >11.8 V on a 12 V system (scaled for 24 V, 36 V, and 48 V).
↓
If that quiet moment never arrives…
2
From 2 days on — it stops waiting for you to disconnect
SOC no longer matters either. Everything else from step 1 still applies.
You'll see  A 10-minute countdown if you are connected.
↓
If it still has not restarted…
3
At 3 days — it restarts even under way and charging
Engine running, charging, connected: none of it defers the restart any longer, and there is no 5-minute wait. Charging is switched off first, then it reboots. Three things still hold it back: a firmware update installing, a guided test or wizard running, or a battery too flat to survive the reboot (below 11.5 V on a 12 V system, scaled for 24 V, 36 V, and 48 V).

One case forces restart quicker than the above schedule: if the regulator finds its own working memory has stayed fragmented for 30 minutes straight, it takes the very next quiet window rather than waiting for the 1-day mark. The step 1 conditions still have to be met.

Nothing is lost in reboot. Settings, history, statistics and anything not yet uploaded are written to storage before it goes down. It comes back about 30 seconds later, still on or off exactly as you left it, and an open dashboard reconnects on its own.

Scheduled Restart Coming
The regulator restarts itself for maintenance, normally at a quiet moment when nobody would notice. It has been running long enough that it will now restart within the next 10 minutes. Charging is switched off first, settings and data are saved, and the device comes back in the same on/off state about 30 seconds later. Starting a guided test or wizard postpones the restart; so does starting the engine, unless it has been running for 3 days.
⚠ Forces upload immediately. Controls may briefly lag.
